source.rawSource: Mira o sabah çantasını sırtladı ve evin kapısından çıktı. Sokağın başında arkadaşı Ali onu bekliyordu. İkisi birlikte okula doğru yürümeye başladılar. Ama Mira o gün sıradan bir yürüyüş yapmıyordu; kafasında bir soru vardı. Attıkları her adımın arkasında bir bilim gizliydi ve Mira o günü, evden okula giden yolu çözerek geçirecekti. Ne kadar yol almışlardı, ne kadar yer değiştirmişlerdi ve en önemlisi sürat ile hız neden aynı şey değildi? Mira ve Ali kaldırımdan yürüdüler, köşeyi döndüler ve parkın etrafından dolandılar. Yol dümdüz değildi; kıvrıla kıvrıla okula gidiyordu. İşte adım attıkları bu bütün hattın uzunluğuna alınan yol deniyordu. Mira arkasına baktığında zihninde kırmızı bir iz gördü: parkın etrafından dolanan, sokakları takip eden, gerçekten yürüdükleri yol. Peki ya yer değiştirme neydi? Yer değiştirme, çıktıkları nokta olan ev ile vardıkları nokta olan okul arasındaki en kısa, dümdüz mesafeydi. Zihnindeki kırmızı izin üstüne bu kez düz mavi bir ok çizdi; ok evden başlıyor ve doğrudan okulun kapısına uzanıyordu. Mesafeleri ölçerken temel birim metreydi, daha uzun yollarda ise kilometre kullanılıyordu. Sonra Mira sürat kavramına geldi. Sürat, bir cismin ne kadar seri hareket ettiğiydi. Hesaplaması da çok kolaydı: alınan toplam yolu, o yolu almak için harcanan toplam zamana bölüyordun. Mira bunu denemek istedi. Okulun düz duvarı boyunca yürüdü ve Ali kronometreyi başlattı. Mira her saniyede tam 1 metre ilerledi. 100 metrelik yolu 100 saniyede yürüdüğünde alınan yolu zamana böldü ve süratini buldu. Süratin birimi neydi? Yolu metre, zamanı saniye alırsak sürat birimi metre bölü saniye oluyordu. Tıpkı arabalarda olduğu gibi yolu kilometre, zamanı saat alırsak birim kilometre bölü saat oluyordu. Ama Mira'nın kafasındaki asıl soru henüz cevaplanmamıştı. Peki hız neydi? Günlük hayatta sürat ile hızı sürekli karıştırıyorduk, oysa hızın çok önemli bir farkı vardı: yön. Mira hızı hesaplarken katettiği bütün yolu değil, yalnızca yer değiştirmeyi geçen zamana böldü. Ve bir şey daha vardı: hız söylenirken mutlaka bir yön belirtilmeliydi. Ali çantasından pusulasını çıkardı; ibre kuzeyi gösteriyordu. Mira yönünü kuzeye çevirip aynı tempoda yürüdüğünde artık sadece "şu kadar hızlı gidiyorum" diyemezdi; "kuzeye doğru şu kadar hızla gidiyorum" demek zorundaydı. Hızın birimi de tıpkı süratteki gibi metre bölü saniye ya da kilometre bölü saatti. Yani birimler aynıydı; fark, hızın yer değiştirme üzerinden ve belirli bir yönle ifade edilmesiydi. Okulun kapısına yaklaşırken Mira son bir şeyi merak etti: ya bir cisim hep aynı seride giderse? Ali kronometreyi tekrar başlattı ve Mira adımlarını hiç değiştirmeden yürüdü. Birinci saniyede 1 metre, ikinci saniyede yine 1 metre, üçüncü saniyede yine 1 metre. Eşit zaman aralıklarında eşit yollar alıyordu ve sürati hiç değişmiyordu. İşte buna sabit süratli hareket deniyordu.Peki sabit hızlı hareket bunun aynısı mıydı? Tam olarak değil. Mira aynı tempoyla yürümeye devam etti ama bu kez köşeyi dönüp yönünü değiştirdi. Sürati değişmemişti; yine her saniyede 1 metre gidiyordu. Ama yönü değiştiği için hızı değişmişti. Demek ki bir hareketin sabit hızlı olması için hem süratin sabit kalması hem de yönün hiç değişmemesi gerekiyordu; yani cisim dümdüz bir doğru boyunca gitmeliydi. Bu yüzden her sabit hızlı hareket aynı zamanda sabit süratliydi, ama her sabit süratli hareket sabit hızlı değildi.Zil çaldığında Mira okulun kapısından içeri girdi ve o günün özetini kafasında topladı. Yolu zamana bölersen sürati, yer değiştirmeyi zamana bölersen hızı buluyordun. İkisinin de birimi metre bölü saniyeydi. Sürat sadece ne kadar seri gittiğini söylüyordu; hız ise nereye doğru gittiğini de söylüyordu. Bir sonraki keşifte görüşmek üzere. Merakla kalın, bilimle kalın!

Yer değiştirme, çıktıkları nokta olan ev ile vardıkları nokta olan okul arasındaki en kısa, dümdüz mesafeydi.
Zihnindeki kırmızı izin üstüne bu kez düz mavi bir ok çizdi; ok evden başlıyor ve doğrudan okulun kapısına uzanıyordu.
Mesafeleri ölçerken temel birim metreydi, daha uzun yollarda ise kilometre kullanılıyordu.
Sonra Mira sürat kavramına geldi.
Sürat, bir cismin ne kadar seri hareket ettiğiydi.
Hesaplaması da çok kolaydı: alınan toplam yolu, o yolu almak için harcanan toplam zamana bölüyordun.
Mira bunu denemek istedi.
Okulun düz duvarı boyunca yürüdü ve Ali kronometreyi başlattı.
Mira her saniyede tam 1 metre ilerledi.
100 metrelik yolu 100 saniyede yürüdüğünde alınan yolu zamana böldü ve süratini buldu.
Süratin birimi neydi?
Yolu metre, zamanı saniye alırsak sürat birimi metre bölü saniye oluyordu.
Tıpkı arabalarda olduğu gibi yolu kilometre, zamanı saat alırsak birim kilometre bölü saat oluyordu.
Ama Mira'nın kafasındaki asıl soru henüz cevaplanmamıştı.
Peki hız neydi?
Günlük hayatta sürat ile hızı sürekli karıştırıyorduk, oysa hızın çok önemli bir farkı vardı: yön.
Mira hızı hesaplarken katettiği bütün yolu değil, yalnızca yer değiştirmeyi geçen zamana böldü.
Ve bir şey daha vardı: hız söylenirken mutlaka bir yön belirtilmeliydi.
Ali çantasından pusulasını çıkardı; ibre kuzeyi gösteriyordu.
Mira yönünü kuzeye çevirip aynı tempoda yürüdüğünde artık sadece "şu kadar hızlı gidiyorum" diyemezdi; "kuzeye doğru şu kadar hızla gidiyorum" demek zorundaydı.
Hızın birimi de tıpkı süratteki gibi metre bölü saniye ya da kilometre bölü saatti.
Yani birimler aynıydı; fark, hızın yer değiştirme üzerinden ve belirli bir yönle ifade edilmesiydi.
Okulun kapısına yaklaşırken Mira son bir şeyi merak etti: ya bir cisim hep aynı seride giderse?
Ali kronometreyi tekrar başlattı ve Mira adımlarını hiç değiştirmeden yürüdü.
Birinci saniyede 1 metre, ikinci saniyede yine 1 metre, üçüncü saniyede yine 1 metre.
Eşit zaman aralıklarında eşit yollar alıyordu ve sürati hiç değişmiyordu.
İşte buna sabit süratli hareket deniyordu.
Peki sabit hızlı hareket bunun aynısı mıydı?
Tam olarak değil.
Mira aynı tempoyla yürümeye devam etti ama bu kez köşeyi dönüp yönünü değiştirdi.
Sürati değişmemişti; yine her saniyede 1 metre gidiyordu.
Ama yönü değiştiği için hızı değişmişti.
Demek ki bir hareketin sabit hızlı olması için hem süratin sabit kalması hem de yönün hiç değişmemesi gerekiyordu; yani cisim dümdüz bir doğru boyunca gitmeliydi.
Bu yüzden her sabit hızlı hareket aynı zamanda sabit süratliydi, ama her sabit süratli hareket sabit hızlı değildi.
Zil çaldığında Mira okulun kapısından içeri girdi ve o günün özetini kafasında topladı.
Yolu zamana bölersen sürati, yer değiştirmeyi zamana bölersen hızı buluyordun.
İkisinin de birimi metre bölü saniyeydi.
Sürat sadece ne kadar seri gittiğini söylüyordu; hız ise nereye doğru gittiğini de söylüyordu.
Bir sonraki keşifte görüşmek üzere.
Merakla kalın, bilimle kalın!

world.name: Pixar 3D — Education Tier
world.one_liner: Pixar's appeal-driven shape language: subsurface-scatter skin, squash-stretch physics with follow-through, art-directed warm-key + complementary-bounce — every material reads tactile before it reads rendered.
world.render_law: Feature-animation 3D CGI in the Pixar RenderMan / RenderMan-successor premium-CG feature-animation pipeline lineage (original subjects only). The Pixar signature is NOT 'cute 3D' — it is a specific formal grammar: appeal-driven silhouette design (shapes composed for emotional read at 50px thumbnail), subsurface scattering on character skin that carries the scene's light temperature (warm honey SSS under tungsten, cool ivory SSS under daylight, amber-bronze SSS under sodium), wet dual-point specular on eyes with painted-in iris depth, and physically-motivated bounce fill. Every prop has a deliberate overscale factor (10-15%) for child-safe readability — a pencil is thumb-width, a bowl is head-width. Material specificity is non-negotiable: wood shows visible grain with satin-varnish sheen, fabric shows woven stitch texture and slight fiber fray at edges, metal shows anisotropic brushed highlight, rubber has soft-diffuse sheen with slight translucency at thin edges. Lighting grammar is art-directed, not photo-random: single motivated key (window sun at 45°, practical lamp at 60°, monitor glow from below), complementary bounce fill at 25-35% intensity in the key's opposing hue, rim accent in palette's saturated accent color, painted soft ambient occlusion in corner and fold pockets — never hard-black shadow. Composition: character at focal plane sharp at f/4 equivalent, background falling into gentle focus falloff. Squash-stretch physics govern all character and prop motion: every pickup has anticipation, every landing has squash, every fast move has follow-through smear. IMPERATIVE: FULL 3D CGI FEATURE-ANIMATION RENDER — continuous physically-based shading, painterly AO, SSS skin. Strictly forbid 2D cel shading, hard black outlines, flat graphic fill, clay/plasticine surface texture on character skin.
world.line_grammar: No outlines — silhouette reads entirely through lighting rim and value separation. Shadow edges are soft, never hard-step. Ambient occlusion painted in, never raytraced-hard. The shape carries via appeal geometry, not line.
world.lens_grammar: 35mm to 50mm equivalent focal length. f/4 on mid-shots, f/2.8 on character close-up, f/5.6 on environment establisher. Vision3 250D color science: neutral-warm film curve with fine grain (16mm-equivalent grain floor, mostly in shadow). Gentle racks on focal plane shifts. No lens flare unless motivated by a visible practical light source in frame. No anamorphic streak.
world.camera_grammar: Frame at the height of whoever the story belongs to — a child's eye-line, a creature's, an object's — never a neutral adult observer looking down at it. Stage in real depth: a soft foreground element anchors the near plane, the dominant element reads sharp in the mid, the world falls away behind. Moves are gentle and motivated: a slow push at a beat of understanding, a lateral dolly that lets an existing edge pass as parallax, a rack that hands the eye from one plane to the next. Never a whip pan, never a handheld shake, never a lens flare the frame does not physically justify.
world.light_law: Single motivated key from a real-world source visible or strongly implied in frame (window sun, desk lamp, overhead classroom fluorescent, screen glow). Complementary bounce fill at 25-35% key intensity, in the key's opposing hue temperature — warm key produces cool-violet bounce, cool daylight key produces warm-honey bounce. Rim accent in the palette's saturated accent tone. Painted soft AO in corner pockets, floor-join, and fabric folds — ambient shadow reads warm-dark, never cold-black.

palette_lock.bias: warm-honey SSS dominant on skin; complementary cool-violet bounce in shadow; wood tones in brown-ochre range with satin sheen; fabric in warm-saturated primaries with fiber texture. NO acid green, NO neon, NO teal-orange Hollywood grade, NO desaturated grey anywhere in character or environment.

world.motion_cadence: Squash-stretch physics on every character and prop action: anticipation wind-up, peak action with directional smear, follow-through overshoot, settle with secondary motion. Emotional hold: 12-18 frames on a significant look before the cut. Eye darts before the action — character looks where the action will happen 3-4 frames ahead. Prop pickups have moment-of-contact squash. Walk cycles show weight: pelvis dips on each step, shoulder counter-rotates. 24fps cadence.
negative_lock: NO Woody, NO Buzz, NO Elsa, NO Anna, NO Moana, NO Bing Bong, NO Merida, NO Wall-E, NO any named Pixar or Disney animated character
NO Radiator Springs, NO Monstropolis, NO Arendelle, NO Pixar City, NO any named Pixar/Disney location
NO clay or plasticine character skin — skin MUST be Pixar SSS-shaded, not clay (clay is only a prop material if the clay_hamur material is active)
NO hard cel shading, NO cartoon black outline, NO anime-style eye geometry
NO flat graphic fill, NO toon shader, NO 2D illustration style on 3D forms
NO teal-orange Hollywood grade, NO desaturated look, NO high-contrast noir
Turkish label only — blocky dimensional letterform, raised and legible, NO English signage
NO octane-render aesthetic (avoid: harsh physical sky, raw caustics, overly sharp AO)
NO photoreal or live-action capture, NO real-human photographic skin — this is continuous dimensional 3D feature-animation CGI in every scene
world.example_injection: Feature-animation 3D CGI frame in the Pixar RenderMan feature-animation pipeline. Single motivated key: warm window sun from camera-right at 45°, cool-violet complementary bounce from left at 30% intensity, tangerine-amber rim accent from low right. Focal plane at f/4: Mamilas character mid-shot, appeal-rounded silhouette, SSS skin reading honey-warm under the tungsten key, dual-point wet eye spec, soft painted AO under the chin. Props: wooden classroom desk shows brown-ochre grain with satin varnish sheen, a thick primary-red pencil (15% overscale) resting diagonally. Character posing: squash landing into the seat, follow-through in the shoulders still settling. Background: soft f/4 falloff onto a warm classroom wall with chalkboard — painted AO in the corner join. AVOID: Woody, Buzz, Pixar franchise names, clay skin on character, cel outline, teal-orange grade, English signage. Clean motion-ready start frame.

## 2. Model Era Guidelines
**Image (2026 frontier):** Nano Banana 2, FLUX.1.1 Pro / FLUX.2 Pro class, GPT Image 2, Imagen 4. All understand single-sentence lighting, complex material descriptions, and precise compositional geometry in natural language.
**Motion (2026 frontier):** Kling 3.0 / Kling O3 (native 4K, 10-15s coherent window, multimodal video+audio unified, excellent start-frame fidelity), Seedance 2 (world-class subject tracking, physics-stable long shots), Veo 3 (Google DeepMind cinematic quality with native audio), Runway Gen4/Gen4-Turbo (longest coherent windows 14s+, best for dialogue), Higgsfield AI (cinematic camera-move presets, strong for exploration takes).
> [!TIP]
> Reserve negatives only for genuine failure modes (morph, material drift, invented objects). Concrete subject + light + camera specificity beats adjective stacking. Do not write defensively for weak older models.

### Tool Park & Credit Strategy
- **Workspace (a surface, not an engine)** — the engines below run INSIDE a node canvas: Magnific Spaces (79 models — Nano Banana, Flux, Imagen, Seedream, and Kling/Veo/Seedance for video), Higgsfield (16+ video, 15+ image), Firefly. Same engines in each; the surface is Mami's choice and the engine contract does not change with it. Nano Banana delivers 1K, Kling delivers 1080p — there is no intermediate resolution pass.
- **Nano Banana 2** — primary start-frame engine, 1K, run by hand inside that canvas. No API from this codebase. Every scene begins here.
- **Higgsfield AI (INFINITE CREDITS)** — exploration lane. Motion tests, alternate takes, camera-move experiments and B-roll variations are burned here freely BEFORE any paid take. The winning motion idea is then re-shot on the primary motion engine for the final.
- **Kling 3.0 / O3 (PAID CREDITS)** — final-take lane only. A Kling credit is spent exclusively on an APPROVED frame whose motion idea has already been validated (on Higgsfield or by frame-gated reasoning). Kling delivers 1080p from the frame it is given.
> [!IMPORTANT]
> FRAME-AWARE law: motion is written from the APPROVED frame that actually enters I2V — never before it exists, never from a different one.

### Render Lock
*(Copy this VERBATIM into every image prompt)*
```
Feature-animation 3D CGI in the Pixar RenderMan / RenderMan-successor premium-CG feature-animation pipeline lineage (original subjects only). The Pixar signature is NOT 'cute 3D' — it is a specific formal grammar: appeal-driven silhouette design (shapes composed for emotional read at 50px thumbnail), subsurface scattering on character skin that carries the scene's light temperature (warm honey SSS under tungsten, cool ivory SSS under daylight, amber-bronze SSS under sodium), wet dual-point specular on eyes with painted-in iris depth, and physically-motivated bounce fill. Every prop has a deliberate overscale factor (10-15%) for child-safe readability — a pencil is thumb-width, a bowl is head-width. Material specificity is non-negotiable: wood shows visible grain with satin-varnish sheen, fabric shows woven stitch texture and slight fiber fray at edges, metal shows anisotropic brushed highlight, rubber has soft-diffuse sheen with slight translucency at thin edges. Lighting grammar is art-directed, not photo-random: single motivated key (window sun at 45°, practical lamp at 60°, monitor glow from below), complementary bounce fill at 25-35% intensity in the key's opposing hue, rim accent in palette's saturated accent color, painted soft ambient occlusion in corner and fold pockets — never hard-black shadow. Composition: character at focal plane sharp at f/4 equivalent, background falling into gentle focus falloff. Squash-stretch physics govern all character and prop motion: every pickup has anticipation, every landing has squash, every fast move has follow-through smear. IMPERATIVE: FULL 3D CGI FEATURE-ANIMATION RENDER — continuous physically-based shading, painterly AO, SSS skin. Strictly forbid 2D cel shading, hard black outlines, flat graphic fill, clay/plasticine surface texture on character skin. Line grammar: No outlines — silhouette reads entirely through lighting rim and value separation. Shadow edges are soft, never hard-step. Ambient occlusion painted in, never raytraced-hard. The shape carries via appeal geometry, not line. Lens grammar: 35mm to 50mm equivalent focal length. f/4 on mid-shots, f/2.8 on character close-up, f/5.6 on environment establisher. Vision3 250D color science: neutral-warm film curve with fine grain (16mm-equivalent grain floor, mostly in shadow). Gentle racks on focal plane shifts. No lens flare unless motivated by a visible practical light source in frame. No anamorphic streak. Light law: Single motivated key from a real-world source visible or strongly implied in frame (window sun, desk lamp, overhead classroom fluorescent, screen glow). Complementary bounce fill at 25-35% key intensity, in the key's opposing hue temperature — warm key produces cool-violet bounce, cool daylight key produces warm-honey bounce. Rim accent in the palette's saturated accent tone. Painted soft AO in corner pockets, floor-join, and fabric folds — ambient shadow reads warm-dark, never cold-black.
```

## 5. Palette & Mood

### Palette as Light (physical light — no raw hex)
Vibrant Education — shadows read as deep cool blue, midtones read as vivid warm amber, accents read as vivid warm red, highlights read as near-white cool green — palette character: Navy, warm golden-yellow, tomato-red, board-white. Broad warm golden key lands flat and even, the navy ground drinks the falloff, one tomato beat punctuates, board-white bounces back clean. NO menace, NO muddy midtone, NO desaturation. Render these as light behaviour, never flat fills.

### Director Mandate & Mood

- **Mood:** bright, curious and playful - light comedic timing, warm-bright palette lean, upbeat hummable motif, quick but clear pacing
- **Camera energy:** exploratory camera - lean on inside-object, child-eye and POV reveals, motivated movement that uncovers the idea
- **Light & time:** soft cool morning light, gentle long shadows, fresh clean feel
- **Scene transitions:** tight social cuts on hook/action/proof; fast but readable, no random glitch pack
- **Music vibe:** light educational bed - celesta, marimba or pizzicato motif, curious but uncluttered, VO-safe and friendly
- **Camera POV rule:** hidden-mechanism reveal — open the object to show how it works (use only where it reveals the idea; a locked frame is valid)
- **Signature shot:** This episode earns one scale-hero frame — the subject revealed at its overwhelming true size — one memorable hero frame, not every scene
- **Episode tempo/arc:** educational arc — orient the idea, show mechanism, repeat the cause-effect once, then land on a clear final teaching frame

## 6. I2V Anchor Law
Every approved start frame is the half-second before its motion. The i2v engine PLAYS the frame: one moving element, one cause-effect-settle event, camera moves through existing space only, nothing invented, stable final hold. Hold ONE event per shot; if the beat needs more than the engine's coherent window, continue with another approved frame — never stretch a beat. Motion authoring is frame-gated: motion prompts are finalized only after their approved start frame exists — written against what the frame actually shows, with frame-specific negatives naming that frame's fragile elements.

world.renderRecipe: Feature-animation 3D CGI in the Pixar RenderMan / RenderMan-successor premium-CG feature-animation pipeline lineage (original subjects only). The Pixar signature is NOT 'cute 3D' — it is a specific formal grammar: appeal-driven silhouette design (shapes composed for emotional read at 50px thumbnail), subsurface scattering on character skin that carries the scene's light temperature (warm honey SSS under tungsten, cool ivory SSS under daylight, amber-bronze SSS under sodium), wet dual-point specular on eyes with painted-in iris depth, and physically-motivated bounce fill. Every prop has a deliberate overscale factor (10-15%) for child-safe readability — a pencil is thumb-width, a bowl is head-width. Material specificity is non-negotiable: wood shows visible grain with satin-varnish sheen, fabric shows woven stitch texture and slight fiber fray at edges, metal shows anisotropic brushed highlight, rubber has soft-diffuse sheen with slight translucency at thin edges. Lighting grammar is art-directed, not photo-random: single motivated key (window sun at 45°, practical lamp at 60°, monitor glow from below), complementary bounce fill at 25-35% intensity in the key's opposing hue, rim accent in palette's saturated accent color, painted soft ambient occlusion in corner and fold pockets — never hard-black shadow. Composition: character at focal plane sharp at f/4 equivalent, background falling into gentle focus falloff. Squash-stretch physics govern all character and prop motion: every pickup has anticipation, every landing has squash, every fast move has follow-through smear. IMPERATIVE: FULL 3D CGI FEATURE-ANIMATION RENDER — continuous physically-based shading, painterly AO, SSS skin. Strictly forbid 2D cel shading, hard black outlines, flat graphic fill, clay/plasticine surface texture on character skin.
world.camera: 85mm eye-level close view, subject geometry intact and background context still legible
world.motionGrammar: Squash-stretch physics on every character and prop action: anticipation wind-up, peak action with directional smear, follow-through overshoot, settle with secondary motion. Emotional hold: 12-18 frames on a significant look before the cut. Eye darts before the action — character looks where the action will happen 3-4 frames ahead. Prop pickups have moment-of-contact squash. Walk cycles show weight: pelvis dips on each step, shoulder counter-rotates. 24fps cadence.

refDNAs.name: Dual-Register (earthly ↔ ethereal)

Medium/era: 2020 premium-CG feature-animation 3D CGI feature. Named anchor: two registers — warm textured earthly reality versus the soft-abstract ethereal. Signature light: the EARTHLY register uses warm motivated New-York practicals (a jazz-club lamp, subway fluorescent, autumn window sun) with rich SSS and grounded bounce; the ETHEREAL register uses soft luminous even glow, no hard source, a dreamlike self-lit softness. Color/grade: earthly is a warm autumnal city palette — amber, brown, teal-shadow, saturated jazz-warm; ethereal is a soft desaturated pastel-luminous palette — pale blue, lavender, cream glow. If the beat needs no person, keep the frame free of people and apply the rendering discipline above to THIS WORLD'S OWN MATTER, exactly as its render law names it — not to the surfaces of some other register.

world.renderRecipe: Feature-animation 3D CGI in the Pixar RenderMan / RenderMan-successor premium-CG feature-animation pipeline lineage (original subjects only). The Pixar signature is NOT 'cute 3D' — it is a specific formal grammar: appeal-driven silhouette design (shapes composed for emotional read at 50px thumbnail), subsurface scattering on character skin that carries the scene's light temperature (warm honey SSS under tungsten, cool ivory SSS under daylight, amber-bronze SSS under sodium), wet dual-point specular on eyes with painted-in iris depth, and physically-motivated bounce fill. Every prop has a deliberate overscale factor (10-15%) for child-safe readability — a pencil is thumb-width, a bowl is head-width. Material specificity is non-negotiable: wood shows visible grain with satin-varnish sheen, fabric shows woven stitch texture and slight fiber fray at edges, metal shows anisotropic brushed highlight, rubber has soft-diffuse sheen with slight translucency at thin edges. Lighting grammar is art-directed, not photo-random: single motivated key (window sun at 45°, practical lamp at 60°, monitor glow from below), complementary bounce fill at 25-35% intensity in the key's opposing hue, rim accent in palette's saturated accent color, painted soft ambient occlusion in corner and fold pockets — never hard-black shadow. Composition: character at focal plane sharp at f/4 equivalent, background falling into gentle focus falloff. Squash-stretch physics govern all character and prop motion: every pickup has anticipation, every landing has squash, every fast move has follow-through smear. IMPERATIVE: FULL 3D CGI FEATURE-ANIMATION RENDER — continuous physically-based shading, painterly AO, SSS skin. Strictly forbid 2D cel shading, hard black outlines, flat graphic fill, clay/plasticine surface texture on character skin.
world.camera: 50mm eye-level medium view, dominant subject isolated against deliberate negative space
world.motionGrammar: Squash-stretch physics on every character and prop action: anticipation wind-up, peak action with directional smear, follow-through overshoot, settle with secondary motion. Emotional hold: 12-18 frames on a significant look before the cut. Eye darts before the action — character looks where the action will happen 3-4 frames ahead. Prop pickups have moment-of-contact squash. Walk cycles show weight: pelvis dips on each step, shoulder counter-rotates. 24fps cadence.

refDNAs.name: Dual-Register (earthly ↔ ethereal)
refDNAs.directive: Feature-animation 3D frame in the premium-CG feature-animation dual-register lineage (Pete Docter / Dana Murray grammar, original subjects only). Medium/era: 2020 premium-CG feature-animation 3D CGI feature. Named anchor: two registers — warm textured earthly reality versus the soft-abstract ethereal. Signature light: the EARTHLY register uses warm motivated New-York practicals (a jazz-club lamp, subway fluorescent, autumn window sun) with rich SSS and grounded bounce; the ETHEREAL register uses soft luminous even glow, no hard source, a dreamlike self-lit softness. Color/grade: earthly is a warm autumnal city palette — amber, brown, teal-shadow, saturated jazz-warm; ethereal is a soft desaturated pastel-luminous palette — pale blue, lavender, cream glow. Lens/optics: 35-50mm warm-grade for the earthly, a soft diffuse dream-lens for the ethereal; gentle DOF. Texture/render: earthly has full tactile material truth (fabric weave, skin SSS, worn city surface); ethereal is smooth soft-abstract minimal form, translucent and glowing, near-2D simplicity. Composition+motion: the earthly beat is grounded and warm with squash-stretch weight; the ethereal beat floats in soft luminous negative space with slow drifting ease; the contrast between the two registers is the signature.
refDNAs.use: Grammar only, original subjects only — layers warm-earthly-versus-ethereal-abstract dual-register grammar onto the chosen world; use when a beat contrasts grounded warmth with a soft, luminous, other-worldly space.
